rows.stimulus:
A function g is defined for -4 ≤ x ≤ 6 except at x = 4. Its graph is described in words below. A closed point is part of the graph. An open circle marks a point that is not on the graph.

1. For -4 ≤ x < -1, the graph is a straight line segment. It starts at the closed point (-4, 0) and ends at an open circle at (-1, 3).
2. At x = -1 there is a single closed point at (-1, 1), so g(-1) = 1.
3. For -1 < x < 2, the graph is a straight line segment. It runs from an open circle at (-1, -2) to an open circle at (2, 4).
4. At x = 2 there is a single closed point at (2, 0), so g(2) = 0.
5. For 2 < x < 4, the graph is an unbroken increasing curve. It starts at the open circle at (2, 4) and rises without bound as x approaches 4 from the left.
6. The vertical line x = 4 is a vertical asymptote, and g(4) is not defined.
7. For 4 < x ≤ 6, the graph is an unbroken decreasing curve. It comes down from arbitrarily large values just to the right of x = 4 and ends at the closed point (6, 1).

rows.stem: Based on electronegativity differences (using the Pauling scale: Cs = 0.79, C = 2.55, H = 2.20, O = 3.44, F = 3.98, N = 3.04), which pair of atoms would be predicted to form a bond with the greatest ionic character?
Which of the following species requires an expanded (greater than octet) valence shell around its central atom in its best Lewis structure?

The nitrite ion, NO2-, is represented by two equivalent resonance contributors in which nitrogen forms one N=O double bond and one N–O single bond (with the negative charge delocalized by resonance). In this Lewis structure, what is the formal charge on the singly-bonded oxygen atom?
What are the electron-domain geometry and molecular (molecular-domain) shape of SF4?

choices.text: Trigonal bipyramidal electron-domain geometry; seesaw molecular shape
Trigonal bipyramidal electron-domain geometry; trigonal pyramidal molecular shape
Octahedral electron-domain geometry; square pyramidal molecular shape
Tetrahedral electron-domain geometry; seesaw molecular shape

rows.stem: Which substance is expected to have the highest normal boiling point?
CH3F and CH3OH have similar molar masses (34 g/mol and 32 g/mol, respectively), yet CH3OH has a substantially higher boiling point (65C) than CH3F (-78C). What best explains this difference?

choices.text: CH3OH molecules are larger, so they experience much stronger London dispersion forces than CH3F.
Intermolecular attractions are limited to dipole-dipole interactions and London dispersion forces because the molecule has no H bonded to N, O, or F.
CH3F is ionic while CH3OH is molecular, so CH3F should have the lower boiling point regardless of intermolecular forces.
Fluorine's higher electronegativity compared to oxygen means CH3F molecules attract each other more strongly, so CH3F should have the higher boiling point.

rows.stem: A solid sample conducts electricity well in both its solid and molten states, is malleable (can be hammered into sheets without shattering), and has a moderately high melting point. What type of solid is this sample most likely to be?

choices.text: An ionic solid, such as an alkali halide
A metallic solid, such as a transition metal
A covalent network solid, such as silicon dioxide
A molecular solid, such as solid iodine

rows.stem: A rigid 2.00 L container holds 0.500 mol of an ideal gas at 27C. What is the pressure of the gas? (R = 0.08206 L*atm/(mol*K))
Separate rigid containers hold samples of He(g) and O2(g) at the same temperature. According to kinetic molecular theory, which statement correctly compares the two samples?

choices.text: The average kinetic energy is the same in both samples, and the average molecular speed is also the same, since both are at the same temperature.
The average kinetic energy is the same in both samples, but He atoms have a greater average speed than O2 molecules.
O2 molecules have greater average kinetic energy than He atoms because O2 has greater mass, and O2 also has greater average speed.
He atoms have greater average kinetic energy than O2 molecules because He moves faster, and O2 has greater average speed.

rows.stem: Under which set of conditions would a real gas be expected to deviate most significantly from ideal gas behavior, and why?

choices.text: High temperature and low pressure, because molecules move so quickly that intermolecular attractions and molecular volume become significant.

Low temperature and high pressure, because molecules are forced close together (making their finite volume non-negligible) and move slowly enough for intermolecular attractive forces to noticeably affect their motion.
High temperature and high pressure, because both factors independently increase the frequency of molecular collisions with the container walls.
Low temperature and low pressure, because the gas volume becomes negligible under these conditions.

rows.stem: As the temperature of water increases, the solubility of a gas such as O2(g) in the water generally decreases. Which statement best explains this observation?

choices.text: At higher temperatures, gas molecules have greater average kinetic energy, allowing more of them to overcome the weak intermolecular attractions holding them in solution and escape into the gas phase.
At higher temperatures, hydrogen bonds between water molecules strengthen, trapping more gas molecules within the solvent structure.
Temperature breaks O2 molecules apart into atoms, so fewer O2 molecules remain dissolved.
The decrease is caused only by evaporation of water, which makes the remaining dissolved oxygen concentration appear lower.

rows.stem: A colored solution has a molar absorptivity of 1.50 x 10^3 M^-1 cm^-1 at its wavelength of maximum absorbance. When placed in a cuvette with a 1.00 cm path length, the solution's absorbance is measured as 0.750. What is the molar concentration of the solution?
A photon of ultraviolet (UV) light is compared to a photon of infrared (IR) light. Which statement correctly ranks their energies and justifies the ranking?

choices.text: The UV photon has more energy than the IR photon because UV light has a shorter wavelength, which corresponds to a higher frequency, and photon energy is directly proportional to frequency (E = hf).
The IR photon has more energy than the UV photon because IR light has a longer wavelength, and longer wavelengths carry more energy.
The two photons have identical energy because all forms of electromagnetic radiation travel at the same speed in a vacuum.
UV photons have more energy because they have a shorter wavelength, and photon energy is directly proportional to wavelength.

rows.stem: A chemist needs to recover acetone (boiling point 56 °C) from a homogeneous mixture of acetone and water (boiling point 100 °C). The two liquids are miscible and do not form an azeotrope. Which technique is most appropriate, and why?

choices.text: Filtration, because it separates the two liquids based on differences in particle size.
Distillation, because heating the mixture selectively vaporizes the lower-boiling acetone, which can then be condensed and collected separately from the higher-boiling water.
Paper chromatography, because it separates substances based on their particle size as they pass through the paper.
Recrystallization, because cooling the mixture causes the higher-boiling liquid to solidify out of solution.

rows.stem: A student dilutes 25.0 mL of a 2.00 M stock solution to a final total volume of 200.0 mL. What is the molarity of the resulting diluted solution?

A student reacts 5.4 g of Al (molar mass 27.0 g/mol) with 3.2 g of O2 (molar mass 32.0 g/mol) according to the balanced equation 4Al(s) + 3O2(g) -> 2Al2O3(s) (molar mass Al2O3 = 102.0 g/mol). What mass of Al2O3 is produced, assuming the reaction goes to completion?

Aqueous solutions of Pb(NO3)2 and KI are mixed, forming a yellow precipitate: Pb(NO3)2(aq) + 2KI(aq) -> PbI2(s) + 2KNO3(aq). Which equation correctly represents the net ionic equation for this reaction?
In the reaction Zn(s) + 2AgNO3(aq) -> Zn(NO3)2(aq) + 2Ag(s), which species is the oxidizing agent, and how does its oxidation state change?

choices.text: Ag+ is the oxidizing agent; its oxidation state decreases from +1 to 0 as it is reduced.
Zn is the oxidizing agent; its oxidation state increases from 0 to +2.
NO3- is the oxidizing agent because nitrogen changes oxidation state during the reaction.
H2O is the oxidizing agent because it supplies oxygen atoms to the reaction.

rows.stem: Which type of chemical reaction is represented by CaCO3(s) -> CaO(s) + CO2(g) upon heating?

choices.text: Decomposition reaction, because a single compound breaks down into two or more simpler substances.
Combination (synthesis) reaction, because two products form from the reactants.
Single-replacement reaction, because calcium changes bonding partners.
Combustion, because CO2 is produced during heating.

rows.stem: A 25.00 mL sample of HCl(aq) is titrated to the equivalence point using 0.100 M NaOH(aq), requiring 32.50 mL of titrant according to HCl(aq) + NaOH(aq) -> NaCl(aq) + H2O(l). What is the concentration of the HCl solution?

Dinitrogen pentoxide decomposes according to the equation 2 N2O5(g) -> 4 NO2(g) + O2(g). At a certain point during the reaction, O2 is forming at a rate of 0.015 M/s. What is the rate of disappearance of N2O5 at that same instant?
The elementary step 2 X(g) + Y(g) -> products is proposed as part of a reaction mechanism. Which rate law is consistent with this elementary step?

A one-step reaction has an activation energy for the forward reaction, Ea(fwd), of 45 kJ/mol and an overall enthalpy change, deltaH, of -20 kJ/mol. What is the activation energy for the reverse reaction, Ea(rev)?
Which of the following correctly describes how a catalyst increases the rate of a chemical reaction?

choices.text: It increases the average kinetic energy of the reactant molecules, so more collisions occur per second.
It provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, increasing the fraction of collisions with sufficient energy to react.
It shifts the reaction equilibrium further toward products.
It increases the magnitude of deltaH, making the reaction more exothermic.

rows.stem: A student dissolves a sample of solid ammonium nitrate in water inside a coffee-cup calorimeter. As the solid dissolves, the temperature of the solution drops from 25.0 C to 18.5 C. Which statement correctly describes this dissolution process?

choices.text: The process is exothermic because the dissolving solid releases heat directly into the solution, which is why the temperature changed.
The process is endothermic; the dissolving ions absorb heat from the surrounding solution, so the solution's own temperature falls, and deltaH for the process is positive.
The process is endothermic, and therefore deltaH for the dissolution must be negative.
The process is exothermic because the water temperature decreases as heat leaves the solution.

rows.stem: Using average bond enthalpies (H-H = 436 kJ/mol, Cl-Cl = 243 kJ/mol, H-Cl = 431 kJ/mol), estimate deltaH for the reaction: H2(g) + Cl2(g) -> 2 HCl(g)

Given standard enthalpies of formation Delta Hf standard: CH4(g) = -74.8 kJ/mol, CO2(g) = -393.5 kJ/mol, H2O(l) = -285.8 kJ/mol, and O2(g) = 0 kJ/mol, calculate Delta H(rxn) for: CH4(g) + 2 O2(g) -> CO2(g) + 2 H2O(l)

Given the following thermochemical equations:
(1) C(s) + O2(g) -> CO2(g), deltaH1 = -393.5 kJ
(2) CO(g) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO2(g), deltaH2 = -283.0 kJ
Use Hess's Law to find deltaH for: C(s) + 1/2 O2(g) -> CO(g)
For the heterogeneous equilibrium CaCO3(s) <-> CaO(s) + CO2(g), which expression correctly represents the equilibrium constant, Kc?
At a given temperature, a reaction has Kc = 4.3 x 10^-9. What does this value indicate about the reaction mixture at equilibrium?

choices.text: At equilibrium, the mixture consists mostly of products.
At equilibrium, the reaction strongly favors reactants.
At equilibrium, reactants and products are present in roughly equal amounts.
The reaction goes essentially to completion, converting all reactants to products.

rows.stem: For N2(g) + 3H2(g) <-> 2NH3(g), Kc = 0.50 at a certain temperature. A reaction mixture is sampled and Qc is calculated to be 2.0. Which statement correctly describes how the system will respond?

choices.text: The reaction will proceed in the forward direction, producing more NH3, because Q is greater than K.
The reaction will proceed in the reverse direction, forming more N2 and H2, because Q greater than K indicates an excess of products relative to the equilibrium ratio.
The system is already at equilibrium, so no net reaction will occur.
The reaction will proceed in the forward direction because Kc is less than 1.

rows.stem:
A saturated aqueous solution of CaF2 is at equilibrium: CaF2(s) <-> Ca2+(aq) + 2F-(aq). A small amount of soluble NaF is added to the solution and stirred until it fully dissolves. What happens to the molar solubility of CaF2?

Assume ideal solution behavior and no complex-ion formation.

choices.text: The molar solubility of CaF2 increases because Na+ removes F- from solution.
The molar solubility of CaF2 decreases because the added F- is a common ion that shifts the equilibrium toward the solid, in accordance with Le Chatelier's principle.
The molar solubility of CaF2 stays the same because Ksp is a constant and is unaffected by adding NaF.
The molar solubility increases because Ksp must increase when more ions are added.

rows.stem: In the reaction HSO4-(aq) + H2O(l) <-> H3O+(aq) + SO4^2-(aq), which species is the conjugate base of HSO4-?
What is the pOH of a 0.0025 M HCl solution at 25 C? (HCl is a strong acid.)
A 0.10 M solution of a weak monoprotic acid HA has Ka = 1.0x10^-5. Assuming the approximation x much less than 0.10 is valid, what is the pH of the solution?

50.0 mL of 0.20 M HCl is mixed with 50.0 mL of 0.30 M NaOH. What is the pH of the resulting solution?

Assume 25 C and additive volumes.
Which of the following hypohalous acids is the strongest acid, and why?

choices.text: HOI, because iodine is the largest halogen and best stabilizes negative charge through its size alone.
HOCl, because chlorine's high electronegativity withdraws electron density inductively through the O-Cl bond, weakening the O-H bond and stabilizing the conjugate base OCl-.
HOI, because iodine forms the strongest binary acid trend and that trend also applies to HOX acids.
HOBr, because bromine is between chlorine and iodine so it should have the intermediate but strongest balance of effects.

rows.stem: During the titration of a weak monoprotic acid with NaOH, the pH at the half-equivalence point is measured to be 4.74. What is the Ka of the acid?
A buffer solution contains 0.30 M sodium acetate (CH3COONa) and 0.15 M acetic acid (CH3COOH), where acetic acid has Ka = 1.8x10^-5 (pKa = 4.74). What is the pH of this buffer?
Four buffer solutions are prepared using the same conjugate acid-base pair (same pKa). Which combination would provide the greatest buffer capacity?

A reaction has deltaH = -92 kJ/mol and deltaS = +198 J/(mol*K). Which statement correctly describes the thermodynamic favorability of this reaction?

Assume Delta H and Delta S remain approximately temperature-independent over the temperature range considered.

choices.text: The reaction is nonspontaneous at all temperatures because deltaH is negative.

The reaction is thermodynamically favorable at all temperatures because deltaG = deltaH - TdeltaS is negative for every value of T greater than 0 when deltaH is less than 0 and deltaS is greater than 0.
The reaction is favorable only at low temperatures because the TdeltaS term becomes negligible as T decreases.
The reaction is favorable only at high temperatures because a large positive deltaS requires a large T to overcome an unfavorable deltaH.

rows.stem: A galvanic cell is built from a Zn electrode in 1.0 M Zn(NO3)2 and a Cu electrode in 1.0 M Cu(NO3)2, connected by a wire and a salt bridge. E standard reduction (Cu2+/Cu) = +0.34 V; E standard reduction (Zn2+/Zn) = -0.76 V. Which statement correctly identifies the cathode and the direction of electron flow?

choices.text: The Cu electrode is the cathode, where Cu2+ is reduced to Cu(s); electrons flow through the external wire from the Zn electrode to the Cu electrode.
The Zn electrode is the cathode because it undergoes oxidation, releasing electrons to the circuit.
Electrons flow from the Zn electrode to the Cu electrode through the salt bridge to complete the circuit.
The Cu electrode is the anode because it has the higher (more positive) standard reduction potential.

rows.stem: A galvanic cell has a cathode half-reaction Ag+ + e- -> Ag(s), E = +0.80 V, and an anode half-reaction Pb(s) -> Pb2+ + 2e-, E(Pb2+/Pb) = -0.13 V. The overall balanced reaction transfers n = 2 mol electrons. What is deltaG for the cell reaction, and is it thermodynamically favorable?

choices.text: deltaG approximately -179 kJ/mol; favorable, since Ecell = Ecathode - Eanode = 0.80 - (-0.13) = +0.93 V and deltaG = -nFE with n = 2.
deltaG approximately +179 kJ/mol; nonfavorable, since Ecell = Eanode - Ecathode = -0.93 V.
deltaG approximately -90 kJ/mol; favorable, using deltaG = -FE with E = 0.93 V.
+179 kJ/mol; nonfavorable, using DeltaG = nFE with E = 0.93 V.

rows.stem: For the cell Zn(s) | Zn2+(aq) || Cu2+(aq) | Cu(s), E°cell = +1.10 V. If [Cu2+] is decreased to well below 1 M while [Zn2+] remains at 1 M, how does the actual cell potential Ecell compare to E standard cell, and why?

choices.text: Ecell decreases below E standard cell, because Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] increases as [Cu2+] decreases, making the -(RT/nF)lnQ term in the Nernst equation more negative.
Ecell increases above E standard cell, because reducing the concentration of any species always increases the cell potential.
Ecell remains equal to E standard cell, because standard reduction potentials are fixed reference values that do not depend on concentration.
Ecell decreases below E standard cell, because Q = [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] decreases as [Cu2+] decreases, making lnQ negative.

rows.stem: A constant current of 2.00 A is passed through molten CaCl2 for 3.00 hours, depositing Ca(s) at the cathode via Ca2+ + 2e- -> Ca(s) (molar mass of Ca = 40.08 g/mol). What mass of Ca(s) is deposited?

choices.text: approximately 4.49 g, from moles e- = (2.00 A x 3.00 x 3600 s) / 96485 C/mol = 0.224 mol e-, moles Ca = 0.224/2 = 0.112 mol, mass = 0.112 mol x 40.08 g/mol.
approximately 8.98 g, from moles e- = 21,600 C / 96485 C/mol = 0.224 mol, treating moles Ca as equal to moles e-.
approximately 2.24 g, from dividing the electron amount by 4 instead of 2.

rows.stem:
The electronegativities of hydrogen and chlorine are given below.

Atom | Electronegativity
H | 2.2
Cl | 3.2

Which statement best describes the H–Cl bond and explains how its bonding electrons are distributed?

choices.text: The bond is polar covalent because Cl attracts the shared electrons more strongly than H, giving Cl a partial negative charge.
The bond is nonpolar covalent because both atoms are nonmetals and therefore share the bonding electrons equally.
The bond is polar covalent because H attracts the shared electrons more strongly than Cl, giving H a partial negative charge.
The bond is ionic because any difference in electronegativity means an electron is completely transferred between the atoms.

rows.stem: A student is given potential energy (PE) data for two hydrogen atoms as a function of internuclear distance. PE is defined as 0 kJ/mol for fully separated atoms. Data (distance in pm, PE in kJ/mol): 40, +250; 60, −380; 74, −436; 100, −360; 150, −150; 300, −5. The student plots internuclear distance on the x-axis. Which description of the correctly drawn graph is accurate?

choices.text: With x in pm and y in kJ/mol, the curve rises steeply below about 50 pm, reaches a minimum at (74 pm, −436 kJ/mol), and levels off toward 0 kJ/mol at large distances.
With x in pm and y in kJ/mol, the curve reaches a minimum at 74 pm and then levels off at −436 kJ/mol at large distances.
With x in pm and y in kJ/mol, the bond length is shown where the curve crosses 0 kJ/mol, near 50 pm, and the minimum marks where the atoms separate.
With x in pm and y in kJ/mol, the curve rises to a maximum of +436 kJ/mol at 74 pm, because energy must be added to break the bond.

rows.stem: A student is constructing a potential-energy-versus-internuclear-distance model comparing a C–C single bond with a C=C double bond. Both curves use zero potential energy for fully separated atoms. How should the student represent the double-bond curve relative to the single-bond curve?

choices.text: Place its minimum at a smaller internuclear distance and a more negative potential energy.
Place its minimum at a greater internuclear distance and a more negative potential energy.
Place its minimum at a smaller internuclear distance and a less negative potential energy.
Place its minimum at the same internuclear distance and a more negative potential energy.

rows.stem: When struck, a crystal of an ionic compound fractures rather than bending. Which explanation best connects this behavior to the arrangement of particles in the solid?

choices.text: The crystal consists of separate neutral molecules whose weak attractions allow them to pull apart when struck.
Displacement of a layer can bring like-charged ions next to one another, and their repulsion causes the crystal to fracture.
Layers of ions slide freely while maintaining their attractive interactions, allowing the crystal to fracture.
Displacement of a layer brings like-charged ions together, and their attraction pulls the crystal apart.

rows.stem: A pure ionic compound has a high melting temperature. Which particle-level model best explains this observation?

choices.text: The solid consists of separate cation–anion pairs; melting requires breaking the strong attraction within every pair.
Cations and anions form a repeating array; the high melting temperature results mainly from the large masses of the ions.
Cations and anions form an extended, repeating array; melting requires substantial energy to disrupt many strong attractions throughout the array.
The solid contains neutral atoms formed when cations and anions lose their charges; strong attractions between these atoms explain its high melting temperature.

rows.stem: A solid alloy contains metals X and Y. Their atomic radii are X: 128 pm and Y: 135 pm. The alloy conducts electricity. Which particulate-level model best explains both the alloy’s structure and its electrical conductivity?

choices.text: Y atoms occupy gaps between X atoms, and mobile, delocalized valence electrons carry current throughout the solid.
Y atoms replace some X atoms at lattice positions, and positive metal ions move through the solid to carry current.
Y atoms replace some X atoms at lattice positions, and valence electrons confined to individual metal atoms carry current throughout the solid.
Y atoms replace some X atoms at lattice positions, and mobile, delocalized valence electrons carry current throughout the solid.

rows.stem: A sample of a pure metal is hammered into a thinner sheet without breaking. Which particulate-level model best explains this observation?

choices.text: Layers of positive metal ions slide past one another while the mobile, delocalized valence electrons continue to hold the solid together.
Layers of alternating positive and negative ions slide past one another while attractions between oppositely charged ions hold the solid together.
The positive metal ions remain in their original positions while the surrounding electron sea becomes thinner and wider.
Layers of metal atoms slide past one another because each atom’s valence electrons remain localized on that atom.

rows.stem: Which description represents a complete, correct Lewis diagram for OH⁻? In every description, the entire structure is enclosed in brackets with a − charge written outside. Each lone pair contains two electrons.

choices.text: One O–H single bond, three lone pairs on O, and no lone pairs on H.
One O–H single bond, two lone pairs on O, and no lone pairs on H.
One O–H single bond and no lone pairs on either atom.
One O=H double bond, two lone pairs on O, and no lone pairs on H.

rows.stem:
The cyanate ion, OCN⁻ (16 valence electrons), has carbon as the central atom. Three candidate Lewis structures are described below. Electronegativity order: O > N > C.

Structure I: O=C=N, with 2 lone pairs on O and 2 lone pairs on N
Structure II: O≡C–N, with 1 lone pair on O and 3 lone pairs on N
Structure III: O–C≡N, with 3 lone pairs on O and 1 lone pair on N

Which claim about the best representation of OCN⁻ is supported by formal-charge reasoning?

choices.text: Structure I, because it has the fewest nonzero formal charges, with only −1 on nitrogen.
Structure III, because its only nonzero formal charge is −1 and it sits on oxygen, the most electronegative atom.
Structure II, because its formal charges add up to −1, matching the charge of the ion.
No structure is best, because the ion rapidly switches among all three structures and spends equal time in each.

rows.stem:
Two samples of element X contain the same two isotopes. Their mass spectra contain only peaks from singly charged monatomic ions.

Isotope mass (amu) | Abundance in sample 1 | Abundance in sample 2
50.0 | 30% | 70%
54.0 | 70% | 30%

Compared with sample 1, how do the average atomic mass and the isotope peak positions change in sample 2?

choices.text: The average atomic mass increases, and the isotope peak positions remain unchanged.
The average atomic mass remains unchanged, and the isotope peak positions remain unchanged.

rows.stem: Aluminum is a Group 13 metal with three valence electrons. Which prediction best explains the formation of its typical monatomic ion?

choices.text: Al³⁻ forms when an aluminum atom loses three valence electrons.
Al³⁺ forms when an aluminum atom loses three valence electrons.
Al⁵⁻ forms when an aluminum atom gains five electrons.
Al⁺ forms when an aluminum atom loses one valence electron.

rows.stem: Silicon nitride, a hard ceramic used in bearings, is a pure compound of silicon and nitrogen. Elemental analysis shows it is 60.06% silicon and 39.94% nitrogen by mass. What is the empirical formula of the compound? (Molar masses: Si = 28.09 g/mol, N = 14.01 g/mol)

In an analysis of a pure oxide of gallium, a student determines that one sample of the compound contains 2.789 g of gallium and 0.955 g of oxygen. Based on these data, what is the empirical formula of the compound? (Molar masses: Ga = 69.72 g/mol, O = 16.00 g/mol)

A colorless liquid used in making optical fibers is a pure compound that contains only germanium and chlorine. The compound is 33.87% germanium by mass. What is the empirical formula of the compound? (Molar masses: Ge = 72.63 g/mol, Cl = 35.45 g/mol)

A chemist measures out a sample of barium nitrate, Ba(NO₃)₂, that contains 2.00 mol of the compound. How many moles of oxygen atoms does the sample contain? (Avogadro's number = 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹)

choices.text: The sample contains 2.00 mol of H atoms.
The sample contains 2.25 mol of H atoms.
The sample contains 0.250 mol of N atoms.

choices.text: The sample contains 1.45 × 10²³ mol of P atoms.

rows.stem: A 5.00 g sample is a mixture of sodium sulfate, Na₂SO₄ (molar mass 142.04 g/mol), and potassium chloride, KCl (molar mass 74.55 g/mol). Elemental analysis shows that the sample contains 0.0300 mol of sodium atoms. What is the percent by mass of Na₂SO₄ in the sample? (Na = 22.99 g/mol)

Both solids dissociate completely. What is the concentration of potassium ion, K⁺, in the solution?

A student dissolves 2.64 g of ammonium sulfate, (NH₄)₂SO₄ (molar mass 132.15 g/mol), and 0.800 g of ammonium nitrate, NH₄NO₃ (molar mass 80.05 g/mol), in water and adds water until the total volume of the solution is 350.0 mL. Both solids dissociate completely. What is the concentration of ammonium ion, NH₄⁺, in the solution?

A student plans to find the molar mass of an unknown gas using PV = nRT. The student weighs an evacuated rigid glass flask whose internal volume has been calibrated as 0.5000 L, fills the flask with the gas, measures the absolute pressure of the gas with a pressure sensor attached to the flask, and weighs the filled flask. The gas is dry, and no liquid is present in the flask at any time. Which additional measurement is needed to calculate the molar mass of the gas?

choices.text: The outside height and diameter of the flask
The vapor pressure of water at room temperature
The temperature of the gas in the flask
The thickness of the flask's glass wall

rows.stem: A student finds the molar mass of a gas from a small cylinder using a gas-tight syringe. The student weighs the empty syringe with its plunger pushed fully in, draws gas from the cylinder into the syringe, closes the tip, and weighs the filled syringe. The plunger slides freely, so the gas in the syringe is at the barometric pressure. The gas is dry, and no liquid is present. The student records: the mass of the empty syringe; the mass of the filled syringe; the gas volume read from the syringe's printed scale; the room temperature in degrees Celsius; the barometric pressure; and the length of the syringe barrel. Which recorded quantity could be left out without affecting the calculated molar mass?

choices.text: The volume read from the printed scale, because the volume can be found from the length of the barrel
The barometric pressure, because the pressure of the gas must instead be found by subtracting the vapor pressure of water
The length of the syringe barrel, because the gas volume is read directly from the printed scale
The room temperature, because a temperature recorded in degrees Celsius cannot be used in PV = nRT

rows.stem: A student releases 0.520 g of a gas from a pressurized can and collects it in an inverted graduated tube that starts out full of water, at 22.0°C. The student then raises or lowers the tube until the pressure of the gas mixture trapped in it matches the barometric pressure, 0.9921 atm, and reads a gas volume of 0.2340 L. Water vapor in the tube contributes a partial pressure equal to the vapor pressure of water, 0.0261 atm at 22.0°C. In the calculation, the student uses 0.9921 atm as the pressure of the collected gas in PV = nRT (R = 0.08206 L·atm/(mol·K)). How does this error affect the calculated molar mass of the gas?

choices.text: It is unchanged, because the water vapor is part of the collected gas, so the barometric pressure is the correct pressure to use.
It is too high, because using the total pressure instead of the gas's partial pressure makes the calculated number of moles of gas too large.
It is too low, because using the total pressure instead of the gas's partial pressure makes the calculated number of moles of gas too large.
It cannot be determined unless the inside diameter of the graduated tube is also known.

rows.stem: To find the percent by mass of water in a sample of damp sand, a student heats the sample in a crucible, lets it cool, and weighs it, repeating the heating-and-cooling cycle. The masses of the crucible and sand after the first three cycles are 24.815 g, 24.702 g, and 24.668 g. What should the student do next?

choices.text: Heat, cool, and weigh the crucible and sand again, repeating until two successive masses agree closely
Discard the sample and repeat the experiment with a sample of a different starting mass
Use the average of the three recorded masses as the final mass
Use 24.668 g as the final mass, because it is the lowest mass recorded

rows.stem: A student wants to find the percent by mass of water in a sample of barium sulfate powder that is still damp with water. The empty crucible has a mass of 16.420 g, and the crucible with the damp sample has a mass of 19.870 g. After three cycles of heating, cooling, and weighing, the masses of the crucible and sample are 19.402 g, 19.355 g, and 19.353 g. Which conclusion is best supported by these data?

choices.text: No percent of water can be stated until the experiment is repeated with a larger starting mass.
The damp sample was 15.0% water by mass.
The damp sample was 14.5% water by mass.
The calculated value is 15.0% water by mass, but the true value is probably lower, because any water not driven off would make the calculated percent too high.

rows.stem: A 6.000 g sample of sodium chloride crystals wet with acetone is placed in a dish of mass 31.250 g and warmed in a drying oven to drive off the acetone, then cooled and weighed. After three warming-and-cooling cycles the masses of the dish and sample are 36.402 g, 36.237 g, and 36.198 g. The student stops here and uses 36.198 g as the final mass to calculate the percent by mass of acetone in the wet sample, obtaining 17.5%. How does the student's result most likely compare with the true percent by mass of acetone?

choices.text: It cannot be judged unless the experiment is repeated with a different starting mass of wet crystals.
It is accurate, because 36.198 g is the lowest mass recorded and is therefore the final mass.
It is too high, because acetone remaining in the crystals is counted as part of the mass lost.
It is too low, because the masses were still decreasing, so some acetone probably remained and the mass lost was too small.

rows.stem: A technician collects 4.40 g of carbon dioxide (44.0 g mol⁻¹) from a fermentation vessel. How many moles of CO₂ were collected?
A student needs 0.400 mol of sodium chloride (58.5 g mol⁻¹) to prepare a saline solution. What mass of NaCl should be weighed out?
A sealed flask contains 1.204 × 10²⁴ molecules of ammonia, NH₃ (17.0 g mol⁻¹). What is the mass of the ammonia in the flask? (Avogadro's number is 6.022 × 10²³ mol⁻¹.)
Four species are listed below. Which one has a trigonal planar molecular geometry around its central atom?
What is the molecular geometry of the nitrate ion, NO₃⁻?
Which species has a trigonal planar molecular geometry, with three identical atoms bonded to the central atom in one plane at bond angles of 120°?
At 298 K, a sample of He gas and a sample of Kr gas are compared. Which statement correctly compares the particles in the two samples?

choices.text: The average kinetic energies are equal, and He particles have the greater average speed.
The average kinetic energies are equal, and Kr particles have the greater average speed.
The Kr particles have the greater average kinetic energy because each particle has a greater mass.
The He particles have the greater average kinetic energy because they move faster on average.

rows.stem: Samples of Ne, N₂, and Cl₂ gas are all at 400 K. Which ranking of average particle speeds, from greatest to least, is correct?
At 300 K, a sample of H₂ (molar mass 2.0 g/mol) and a sample of O₂ (molar mass 32 g/mol) are compared. Which statement correctly compares the average particle speeds?

choices.text: H₂ particles are 4 times as fast as O₂ particles.
H₂ particles are 16 times as fast as O₂ particles.
H₂ particles are one-fourth as fast as O₂ particles.
H₂ and O₂ particles have the same average speed.

What is the ground-state electron configuration of the Mn2+ ion (Mn, Z = 25, ground-state configuration [Ar]3d^5 4s^2)?

A chemist records the photoelectron spectrum of a neutral gaseous atom. In order of decreasing binding energy, the six peaks have relative areas 2, 2, 6, 2, 6, and 1. Which element produced the spectrum?
The photoelectron spectrum of a neutral atom has five peaks. From highest to lowest binding energy, their relative areas are 2, 2, 6, 2, and 3. Identify the element.
A neutral atom's photoelectron spectrum is predicted to show exactly three peaks, in the relative-area ratio 2 : 2 : 1 from highest to lowest binding energy. Which element fits this prediction?
The first ionization energy of beryllium (899 kJ/mol) is greater than that of boron (801 kJ/mol), even though boron has a higher nuclear charge. Which statement correctly explains this trend?

choices.text: Beryllium's outermost electrons are in a filled 2s subshell, while boron's outermost electron occupies the higher-energy 2p subshell, which is partly shielded by the 2s² electrons and is therefore removed more easily.
Boron's atomic radius is larger than beryllium's, so its outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and is removed more easily than beryllium's electrons.
Boron's outermost electron is shielded by the 1s electrons, but beryllium's outermost electrons are not, so beryllium's electrons feel a larger effective nuclear charge.
Boron has the greater nuclear charge, so its outermost electron is always held more tightly than the outermost electrons of beryllium, whatever subshell it is in.

rows.stem: The first ionization energy of zinc (906 kJ/mol) is greater than that of gallium (579 kJ/mol), even though gallium has a higher nuclear charge. Which statement correctly explains this trend?

choices.text: Gallium's outermost electron is in a higher principal shell than zinc's outermost electrons, so it is much farther from the nucleus and is removed more easily.
Gallium has the greater nuclear charge, so its outermost electron is always held more tightly than the outermost electrons of zinc, whatever subshell it is in.
Zinc's 3d subshell is only partly filled, and this partial filling holds its 4s electrons more tightly than gallium's 4p electron is held.

Zinc's outermost electrons are in a filled 4s subshell, while gallium's outermost electron occupies the higher-energy 4p subshell, which is shielded by the 4s² electrons and is therefore removed more easily.

rows.stem: The first ionization energy of nitrogen (1402 kJ/mol) is greater than that of oxygen (1314 kJ/mol), even though oxygen has a higher nuclear charge. Which statement correctly explains this trend?

choices.text: Oxygen has the greater nuclear charge, so its outermost electron is always held more tightly than the outermost electrons of nitrogen, whatever the arrangement.
Nitrogen's three 2p electrons occupy separate orbitals, while oxygen has one 2p orbital holding two electrons, and the repulsion between that pair makes an oxygen electron easier to remove.
Oxygen's atomic radius is larger than nitrogen's, so its outermost electron is farther from the nucleus and is removed more easily than nitrogen's electrons.
Oxygen's outermost electron occupies a 3p subshell, which is higher in energy and shielded by the 2p electrons, so it is removed more easily than nitrogen's.

rows.stem: A student compares four bonds using Pauling electronegativities (Na = 0.93, H = 2.20, S = 2.58, N = 3.04, Cl = 3.16, O = 3.44). Which bond is predicted to have the greatest ionic character?
Using Pauling electronegativities (K = 0.82, Si = 1.90, P = 2.19, H = 2.20, S = 2.58, Br = 2.96, Cl = 3.16), which ranking lists the bonds in order of INCREASING ionic character?

A student is asked to predict which bond in a set will behave most like an ionic interaction. Pauling electronegativities: Li = 0.98, Be = 1.57, C = 2.55, Cl = 3.16, I = 2.66, O = 3.44, F = 3.98. Which bond has the greatest ionic character?
In its best Lewis structure, which species has a central atom surrounded by more than eight electrons?
In the best Lewis structure of IF₅, how many electrons surround the central iodine atom?
Which ion requires its central atom to hold more than eight electrons in its best Lewis structure?
In one resonance contributor of ozone, O₃, the central oxygen atom forms one O=O double bond and one O–O single bond and carries one lone pair. What is the formal charge on the central oxygen atom?
In the Lewis structure of the nitrate ion, NO₃⁻, nitrogen forms one N=O double bond and two N–O single bonds and has no lone pairs. What is the formal charge on nitrogen?
In the Lewis structure of carbon monoxide, CO, the atoms are joined by a triple bond and each atom has one lone pair. What is the formal charge on the carbon atom?
What is the molecular shape of XeF₄?
What is the molecular shape of BrF₃?
A molecule has a central atom with six electron domains and a square pyramidal molecular shape. Which formula could represent the molecule?
Of the following liquids, which is expected to have the highest normal boiling point?
Hydrogen fluoride has a much higher normal boiling point than hydrogen chloride. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.text: Hydrogen bonds form between HF molecules and are stronger than the attractions between HCl molecules.
The H–F bond is stronger than the H–Cl bond, so more energy is needed to vaporize HF.
HF has the greater molar mass, so its London dispersion forces are stronger than those in HCl.
HCl is nonpolar, so only weak London dispersion forces act between HCl molecules.

rows.stem: At 1 atm, which of these substances is expected to condense at the highest temperature?

Ethanol (CH3CH2OH) and dimethyl ether (CH3OCH3) are isomers, so each has a molar mass of 46 g/mol. Ethanol boils at 78°C, whereas dimethyl ether boils at -24°C. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.text: Ethanol has an H atom bonded to O, so its molecules hydrogen bond to one another; the H atoms in dimethyl ether are bonded only to C.
Every H atom in dimethyl ether can hydrogen bond, but the O-H hydrogen bonds in ethanol are considerably stronger.
Ethanol has much stronger London dispersion forces because its molecules are larger and more polarizable than those of dimethyl ether.
Dimethyl ether is nonpolar, so it has only London dispersion forces, whereas the polar ethanol also has dipole-dipole forces.

rows.stem: H2O has a molar mass of 18 g/mol, and H2S has a molar mass of 34 g/mol. Even so, H2O boils at 100°C while H2S boils at -60°C. Which statement best explains why H2O has the much higher boiling point?

choices.text: H2O molecules form hydrogen bonds with one another because H is bonded to O, whereas H2S has no H bonded to N, O, or F.
Boiling H2O requires breaking the O-H covalent bonds, which are stronger than the S-H bonds in H2S.
H2S has the larger molar mass, so its molecules attract one another more strongly and H2S should have the higher boiling point.
H2O has the stronger London dispersion forces because oxygen is more electronegative than sulfur.

rows.stem: Methylamine (CH3NH2, 31 g/mol) boils at -6°C, while ethane (CH3CH3, 30 g/mol) boils at -89°C. Which statement best explains why methylamine has the higher boiling point?

choices.text: Ethane has C-H bonds that form hydrogen bonds, but the N-H hydrogen bonds in methylamine are considerably stronger than these.
The N-H covalent bonds in methylamine must be broken when it boils, and these are much stronger than the C-C bond in ethane.
Methylamine has a slightly greater molar mass than ethane, so its London dispersion forces are much stronger than those of ethane.
Methylamine molecules hydrogen bond through their N-H groups, whereas ethane molecules are held together only by London dispersion forces.

rows.stem: A solid is very hard and brittle and melts above 1,700°C. It does not conduct electricity as a solid, and it does not conduct electricity when molten. What type of solid is this sample most likely to be?

choices.text: A metallic solid, such as tungsten metal
A molecular solid, such as solid carbon dioxide
An ionic solid, such as magnesium oxide
A network solid, such as silicon carbide

rows.stem: A white crystalline solid shatters when struck with a hammer and melts at 801°C. The solid does not conduct electricity, but it conducts electricity well after it is melted. What type of solid is this sample most likely to be?

choices.text: An ionic solid, such as sodium chloride
A metallic solid, such as copper
A covalent network solid, such as quartz
A molecular solid, such as sucrose

rows.stem: A yellow solid is soft, melts at 119°C, and dissolves in nonpolar solvents. It does not conduct electricity as a solid or as a liquid. What type of solid is this sample most likely to be?

choices.text: An ionic solid, such as potassium bromide
A covalent network solid, such as diamond
A molecular solid, such as solid sulfur
A metallic solid, such as lead

rows.stem: A rigid 5.00 L tank holds 0.250 mol of argon gas at 47°C. What is the pressure of the gas? (R = 0.08206 L*atm/(mol*K))

A flexible container holds 0.800 mol of helium gas at 2.50 atm and 25°C. What is the volume of the container? (R = 0.08206 L*atm/(mol*K))
Samples of H2(g) and CO2(g) are in separate flasks at 300 K. Which statement about the molecules in the two samples is correct?

choices.text: The average kinetic energy and the average speed are both the same for the two samples because the temperatures are the same.
The CO2 molecules have the greater average kinetic energy because they are more massive, and they move faster on average.
The average kinetic energy is the same for both samples, and the H2 molecules move faster on average than the CO2 molecules.
The H2 molecules have the greater average kinetic energy because they move faster, so the two samples are at different temperatures.

rows.stem: A rigid container holds helium gas at 300 K. The gas is heated to 600 K. Which statement correctly describes the change in the average kinetic energy and the average speed of the helium atoms?

choices.text: The average kinetic energy doubles, and the average speed also doubles.
The average kinetic energy increases by a factor of about 1.4, and the average speed increases by a factor of about 1.4.
The average kinetic energy doubles, and the average speed stays the same because the mass of each atom is unchanged.
The average kinetic energy doubles, and the average speed increases by a factor of about 1.4.

rows.stem: A rigid vessel at 400 K contains a mixture of helium (4.0 g/mol) and argon (40 g/mol). Which statement about the gases is correct?

choices.text: The average kinetic energy is the same for both gases, and the helium atoms move about 3 times faster on average than the argon atoms.
Because both gases are in the same vessel at the same temperature, they have the same average kinetic energy and the same average speed.
The argon atoms have about 10 times the average kinetic energy of the helium atoms, and the two gases have the same average speed.
The average kinetic energy is the same for both gases, and the helium atoms move about 10 times faster on average than the argon atoms.

rows.stem: A student wants carbon dioxide gas to behave as nearly like an ideal gas as possible. Which set of conditions is best, and why?

choices.text: 250 K and 50 atm, because the molecules collide more often, which makes the gas obey kinetic molecular theory more closely.
250 K and 0.50 atm, because low pressure alone is enough to make any gas behave ideally at any temperature.
450 K and 0.50 atm, because the molecules are fast and far apart, so attractions and molecular volume are negligible.
450 K and 50 atm, because high temperature alone is enough to make any gas behave ideally at any pressure.

rows.stem: At 1 atm and 298 K, the measured pressure of an ammonia (NH3, 17 g/mol) sample is lower than the ideal gas law predicts by a larger percentage than for the same amount of methane (CH4, 16 g/mol) in the same container. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.text: NH3 is slightly more massive than CH4, so its molecules move much more slowly and exert noticeably less pressure on the walls.
NH3 molecules are much larger than CH4 molecules, so their own volume takes up more of the container and lowers the pressure.
The stronger attractions between NH3 molecules pull them together, so they strike the walls less forcefully and the pressure is lower.
The attractions between NH3 molecules pull them toward the walls of the container, which increases the pressure above the ideal value.

rows.stem: A rigid flask contains nitrogen gas that behaves nearly ideally at 300 K. When the flask is cooled to 80 K, near the boiling point of N2, the measured pressure is lower than the ideal gas law predicts. Which statement best explains why?

choices.text: At 80 K the molecules stop moving entirely, so the pressure falls to nearly zero regardless of what the ideal gas law predicts.
At 80 K the slower N2 molecules attract one another noticeably, so they strike the walls less forcefully than ideal particles would.
At 80 K the N2 molecules become polar and develop permanent dipoles, so strong dipole-dipole forces act between them.
At 80 K the volume of the N2 molecules is no longer negligible, so the available volume is smaller and the pressure drops below ideal.

rows.stem: Two identical bottles of soda are opened at the same time and left open to the air. One sits in a refrigerator at 4 °C and the other sits on a table at 22 °C. After an hour, the warmer soda has lost noticeably more of its dissolved CO₂(g) and tastes flatter. Which statement best explains this observation?

choices.text: Warmer water has stronger hydrogen bonding between its molecules, which squeezes the CO₂ molecules out of the solution as the water structure tightens.
Warmer CO₂ molecules have greater average kinetic energy, so more of them overcome their weak attractions to water molecules and escape from the solution into the gas phase.
Heat breaks CO₂ molecules apart into carbon and oxygen atoms, so fewer CO₂ molecules remain dissolved in the warm soda.
The warm soda loses CO₂ only because more water evaporates, which carries CO₂ away; the solubility of CO₂ itself does not depend on temperature.

rows.stem: Environmental scientists find 11.9 mg/L of dissolved O₂ in a river at 8 °C upstream of a power plant and only 7.8 mg/L at 28 °C downstream, where heated cooling water has warmed the river. The air above both sites has the same pressure and the same O₂ content. Which statement best explains the lower dissolved oxygen downstream?

choices.text: Heating makes each O₂ molecule expand, so each one takes up more space and fewer of them fit between the water molecules downstream.
Dissolving a gas absorbs energy, so heating should favor dissolving more O₂; the downstream drop must be caused entirely by organisms using up the oxygen.
At the higher temperature, dissolved O₂ molecules have greater average kinetic energy, so more of them break free of their weak attractions to water and enter the air above the river.
Water vapor from the warmer river displaces O₂ from the air above it, so less O₂ is available to dissolve in the downstream water.

rows.stem: Surface ocean water near the poles (about 2 °C) contains more dissolved CO₂(g) than surface water near the equator (about 28 °C), even though the air above both regions has the same pressure and the same composition. Which statement best explains this difference?

choices.text: At low temperature, CO₂ molecules become more polar, so they are attracted more strongly to the polar water molecules around them.
Colder water forms stronger ion-dipole attractions with CO₂ molecules, and these attractions hold the CO₂ in solution.
Colder water is denser, and the extra weight of the water above pushes more CO₂ gas down into the solution.
In the colder water, CO₂ molecules have lower average kinetic energy, so fewer of them overcome their weak attractions to water and escape, and more CO₂ stays dissolved.

rows.stem: A spectrophotometer set to the wavelength of maximum absorbance gives an absorbance of 0.360 for a dye solution in a cuvette with a 1.00 cm path length. The molar absorptivity of the dye at this wavelength is 2.40 x 10^4 M^-1 cm^-1. What is the molar concentration of the dye?

A chemist measures a solution of a colored complex ion in a cuvette with a 2.00 cm path length at the complex's wavelength of maximum absorbance and records an absorbance of 0.425. At this wavelength the molar absorptivity of the complex is 8.50 x 10^2 M^-1 cm^-1. What is the concentration of the complex?

A 2.50 x 10^-5 M solution of an organic dye has an absorbance of 0.600 at its wavelength of maximum absorbance, where its molar absorptivity is 1.20 x 10^4 M^-1 cm^-1. What is the path length of the cuvette used?

A blue laser pointer emits photons of wavelength 450 nm, and a red laser pointer emits photons of wavelength 650 nm. Which statement correctly compares the energy of a single photon from each laser and justifies the comparison?

choices.text: A blue photon has more energy than a red photon because its shorter wavelength corresponds to a higher frequency, and photon energy is directly proportional to frequency (E = hν).
A red photon has more energy than a blue photon because its longer wavelength corresponds to a lower frequency, and photon energy is inversely proportional to frequency.
A blue photon has more energy than a red photon because it has a shorter wavelength, and photon energy is directly proportional to wavelength.
The two photons have equal energy because both lasers emit visible light that travels at \(3.00\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m/s}\) in a vacuum.

rows.stem: A dental X-ray machine produces photons of wavelength about 0.1 nm, and a household microwave oven produces photons of wavelength about 12 cm. Assume the microwave oven's beam is far more intense (it delivers more total energy each second) than the X-ray beam. Which statement correctly compares the energy of a single photon of each type?

choices.text: A single microwave photon carries more energy than a single X-ray photon, because a 12 cm wave is physically larger than a 0.1 nm wave and larger waves carry more energy.
A single microwave photon carries more energy than a single X-ray photon, because the microwave beam is more intense and delivers more total energy.
A single X-ray photon carries more energy than a single microwave photon, because shorter-wavelength radiation travels faster through a vacuum.
A single X-ray photon carries far more energy than a single microwave photon, because its far shorter wavelength means a far greater frequency (c = λν) and E = hν.

rows.stem: Photon P has a wavelength of 5.0 x 10^-7 m. Photon Q has a frequency of 4.0 x 10^14 s^-1. (Take the speed of light as 3.0 x 10^8 m/s.) Which statement correctly compares the energies of the two photons?

choices.text: The two photons have equal energy, because both travel at \(3.0\times10^{8}\,\mathrm{m/s}\) in a vacuum regardless of wavelength or frequency.
Photon Q has more energy, because its given value of \(4.0\times10^{14}\) is numerically far larger than the \(5.0\times10^{-7}\) given for photon P.
Photon Q has about 1.5 times the energy of photon P, because \(\lambda=c/\nu=7.5\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}\) for Q, which is longer than \(5.0\times10^{-7}\,\mathrm{m}\) for P.
Photon P has about 1.5 times the energy of photon Q, because \(\nu=c/\lambda=6.0\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\) for P, which is greater than \(4.0\times10^{14}\,\mathrm{s^{-1}}\) for Q.

rows.stem: A chemist needs to recover hexane (boiling point 69 °C) from a homogeneous mixture of hexane and toluene (boiling point 111 °C). The two liquids are nonpolar, fully miscible, and do not form an azeotrope. Which technique is most appropriate, and why?

choices.text: Distillation, because hexane's weaker London dispersion forces give it the lower boiling point, so heating vaporizes it first and its condensed vapor is collected separately.
Recrystallization, because cooling the mixture to room temperature makes the lower-boiling hexane crystallize out of solution.
Separation with a separatory funnel, because the less dense hexane floats as its own layer that can be drained apart from the toluene.
Filtration, because the smaller hexane molecules pass through the filter paper while the larger toluene molecules are held back.

rows.stem: In a paper chromatography experiment, a mixture of two pigments, X and Y, is spotted near the bottom of a strip of polar cellulose paper. The strip is placed in a nonpolar solvent that rises up the paper. After the run, pigment Y has traveled much farther up the paper than pigment X. Which statement best explains why Y traveled farther?

choices.text: Y is more polar than X, so it dissolves better in the solvent that rises up the paper and is carried farther.
Y is less polar than X, so the polar paper holds it less strongly and the nonpolar solvent carries it farther.
Y has stronger attractions to the paper than X does, and the paper carries it upward along with the rising solvent.
Y has smaller particles than X, so it passes through the pores of the paper more easily, as in filtration.

rows.stem: A student pours a clear blue solution of CuSO₄(aq) through filter paper into a clean flask, hoping to collect the CuSO₄ on the paper. The filtrate in the flask is still blue and the paper holds back nothing. Which statement best explains this result?

choices.text: The dissolved Cu²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions are individually dispersed among water molecules and are far smaller than the pores in the paper, so they pass through with the water.
Filtration separates liquids from other liquids according to density, so it cannot affect a solute that is dissolved in the liquid.
The pores in the filter paper were too large for this solute, and a finer-pore filter would have trapped the Cu²⁺ and SO₄²⁻ ions on the paper.
Filtration separates substances by polarity, and the polar water and the ionic CuSO₄ both pass through the polar filter paper together.

rows.stem: A technician transfers 10.0 mL of 6.00 M HCl(aq) into a volumetric flask and adds water until the solution reaches the 250.0 mL mark. What is the molarity of the diluted acid?
A student must prepare 250.0 mL of 0.600 M KNO₃(aq) by diluting a 3.00 M stock solution with water. What volume of the stock solution should be measured out?
A student adds 85.0 mL of distilled water to 15.0 mL of 0.800 M KMnO₄(aq) and mixes thoroughly, assuming the volumes are additive. What is the molarity of the resulting solution?

Methanol, CH₃OH, contains a single bond between a carbon atom and an oxygen atom. The electronegativity values are shown in the table below.

Atom | Electronegativity
C | 2.6
O | 3.4

Which claim about the C–O bond in methanol, including its justification, is best supported by these data?

choices.text: The C–O bond is nonpolar covalent because carbon and oxygen are both nonmetals, so they share the bonding electrons equally.
The C–O bond is polar covalent because C pulls the shared electron pair more strongly than O does, so C carries a partial negative charge.
The C–O bond is polar covalent because O pulls the shared electron pair more strongly than C does, so O carries a partial negative charge.
The C–O bond is ionic because any difference in electronegativity means an electron is completely transferred from C to O.

rows.stem: A chemistry student models the bond in a Cl₂ molecule using calculated potential energy values for two chlorine atoms at several internuclear distances. The potential energy of two completely separated Cl atoms is set at 0 kJ/mol. Data (internuclear distance in pm, potential energy in kJ/mol): 150, +300; 180, −150; 199, −242; 230, −200; 300, −80; 500, −3. The student will put internuclear distance on the horizontal axis. Which statement correctly describes the graph the student should draw?

choices.text: With distance in pm and energy in kJ/mol, the curve bottoms out at 199 pm and then flattens at −242 kJ/mol as the distance keeps increasing.
With distance in pm and energy in kJ/mol, the curve climbs steeply at distances below about 180 pm, bottoms out at (199 pm, −242 kJ/mol), and flattens toward 0 kJ/mol at large distances.
With distance in pm and energy in kJ/mol, the bond length is shown where the curve crosses 0 kJ/mol, near 170 pm, and the lowest point marks where the atoms separate.
With distance in pm and energy in kJ/mol, the curve rises to a peak of +242 kJ/mol at 199 pm, because energy must be added to break the bond.

rows.stem: For a lab report, a student sketches two potential-energy-versus-internuclear-distance curves on one set of axes: one for the N–N single bond in hydrazine and one for the N≡N triple bond in nitrogen gas. Potential energy is set to zero for fully separated atoms. How should the student draw the triple-bond curve compared with the single-bond curve?

choices.text: Its minimum should sit at a shorter internuclear distance and lie farther below zero.
Its minimum should sit at a longer internuclear distance and lie farther below zero.
Its minimum should sit at a shorter internuclear distance and lie closer to zero.
Its minimum should sit at the same internuclear distance and lie farther below zero.

rows.stem: A student taps a small chisel against a crystal of potassium bromide, KBr. Instead of flattening or denting, the crystal shatters into smaller pieces with flat faces. Which particle-level explanation best accounts for this observation?

choices.text: Solid KBr is made of individual neutral KBr molecules held together by weak forces, so the molecules separate easily when the crystal is struck.
The blow shifts one plane of ions relative to the next so that K⁺ ions sit beside K⁺ ions and Br⁻ beside Br⁻, and the resulting repulsion splits the crystal.
Planes of K⁺ and Br⁻ ions glide past one another while each ion keeps oppositely charged neighbors, so the crystal breaks apart.
Shifting a plane of ions places like-charged ions side by side, and the attraction between those like charges pulls the crystal apart.

rows.stem: Magnesium oxide, MgO, is used to line furnaces because it can remain solid while metals inside the furnace are molten. Which particle-level explanation best accounts for the lining’s resistance to melting?

choices.text: MgO consists of individual Mg²⁺–O²⁻ pairs, and the strong attraction inside each independent pair makes the lining difficult to melt.
Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions occupy a repeating lattice, but their large particle masses are the main reason the lining resists melting.
The positive and negative charges cancel within MgO, leaving neutral atoms whose strong mutual attractions prevent the lining from melting.
Mg²⁺ and O²⁻ ions occupy a repeating three-dimensional lattice whose numerous strong electrostatic attractions require considerable energy to disrupt.

rows.stem: A steel wire carries current in an electrical circuit. The steel consists mainly of iron with a small amount of carbon added. For this model, the atomic radii are 126 pm for iron and 77 pm for carbon. Which description connects the wire’s alloy structure with its ability to conduct electricity?

choices.text: Carbon atoms substitute for iron atoms at lattice sites; delocalized valence electrons move through the wire and transport charge.
Carbon atoms fit into spaces within the iron framework; positive iron ions travel through the wire and transport charge.
Carbon atoms fit into spaces within the iron framework; delocalized valence electrons move through the wire and transport charge.
Carbon atoms fit into spaces within the iron framework; valence electrons remain attached to individual iron atoms while transporting charge through the wire.

rows.stem: A straight wire made of pure copper is bent into a loop without cracking. Which particulate-level description best accounts for the wire’s ability to change shape while remaining intact?

choices.text: Positive and negative copper ions shift relative to one another, while attractions between these oppositely charged ions keep the wire intact.
Positive copper ions stay at their original locations, while only the surrounding electron sea curves into the wire’s new shape.
Copper atoms shift relative to one another, while valence electrons confined to their individual atoms keep the wire intact.
Positive copper ions shift relative to one another, while mobile valence electrons distributed throughout the solid maintain attractions that hold it together.

rows.stem: The amide ion, NH₂⁻, has nitrogen as its central atom. Which description gives a complete, correct Lewis diagram for this ion? Assume each description shows the whole structure inside brackets with a − charge written outside, and that every lone pair holds two electrons.

choices.text: Two N–H single bonds, one lone pair on N, and no lone pairs on either H.
Two N–H single bonds, two lone pairs on N, and no lone pairs on either H.
Two N–H single bonds and no lone pairs on any atom.
One N=H double bond, one N–H single bond, one lone pair on N, and no lone pairs on either H.

rows.stem: The thiocyanate ion, SCN⁻, has 16 valence electrons and a central carbon atom. Three candidate Lewis structures are listed. Structure I: S=C=N, with 2 lone pairs on S and 2 lone pairs on N. Structure II: S≡C–N, with 1 lone pair on S and 3 lone pairs on N. Structure III: S–C≡N, with 3 lone pairs on S and 1 lone pair on N. Electronegativities increase in the order C < S < N. Which claim about the best Lewis representation of SCN⁻ does formal-charge reasoning support?

choices.text: Structure III, because it has only one nonzero formal charge, −1 on sulfur.
Structure II, because its formal charges sum to −1, equal to the charge of the ion.
Structure I, because its only nonzero formal charge is −1, located on nitrogen, the most electronegative atom.
None of the structures is best, because the ion rapidly flips among all three and spends equal time in each.

rows.stem: A laboratory uses mass spectrometry to analyze a purified batch of boron. The spectrum shows two peaks, both produced by singly charged monatomic ions. Use the following rounded isotope masses: lighter isotope, 10.0 amu; heavier isotope, 11.0 amu. The batch has an average atomic mass of 10.7 amu. If p denotes the fractional abundance of the lighter isotope, which equation correctly relates p to the average atomic mass?

A chemist records the mass spectrum of a pure sample of element X. Every peak comes from a singly charged monatomic ion, and each peak height is scaled so that the largest peak equals 100. The data are: isotope mass 28.0 u, relative height 100; isotope mass 29.0 u, relative height 15.0; isotope mass 30.0 u, relative height 10.0. What average atomic mass of X do these data give?

Fluorine and chlorine belong to group 17. To represent calcium chloride using a particle model of CaF₂, a student substitutes one Cl⁻ ion for each F⁻ ion and keeps the Ca²⁺ ions. The resulting representation has one Ca²⁺ ion for every two Cl⁻ ions. Does this representation agree with typical ionic bonding?

choices.text: No; the subscript 2 in CaCl₂ requires each chloride ion to have a −2 charge.
No; chlorine typically loses one electron to form Cl⁺, making all the modeled ions positively charged.
Yes; fluorine and chlorine typically form ions with identical charges, so the substitution maintains electrical neutrality.
No; an electrically neutral model must contain equal numbers of calcium ions and chloride ions.

rows.stem: A fireworks designer uses a strontium salt to produce a red flame. Strontium is a Group 2 metal with two valence electrons. Which statement best predicts the charge of the monatomic ion strontium forms in its salts and explains how that charge arises?

choices.text: Sr²⁻ forms when a strontium atom loses its two valence electrons.
Sr²⁺ forms when a strontium atom loses its two valence electrons.
Sr⁶⁻ forms when a strontium atom gains six electrons.
Sr⁺ forms when a strontium atom loses one valence electron.

rows.stem: A mass spectrum of a sample of element Z shows exactly two peaks: one at mass 69.0 u with a relative abundance of 60.0%, and one at mass 71.0 u with a relative abundance of 40.0%. The peaks come from singly charged monatomic ions. What is the average atomic mass of Z?
Analysis of a pure hydrocarbon shows 85.7% carbon and 14.3% hydrogen by mass. Its molar mass is 56 g/mol. What is its molecular formula? (Use C = 12 g/mol and H = 1 g/mol.)

A uniform-looking white powder is analyzed in three independent samples. Sample 1 contains 3.00 g of element X and 2.00 g of element Y. Sample 2 contains 4.89 g of X and 3.00 g of Y. Sample 3 contains 2.76 g of X and 2.00 g of Y. Which conclusion do these data best support?

choices.text: The powder is a mixture, because the X-to-Y mass ratio (1.50, 1.63, 1.38) changes from sample to sample.
The powder is a pure substance, because it looks uniform throughout.
The powder is a pure compound whose formula changes with the size of the sample.
The powder is a pure substance, because it contains only two elements.

rows.stem: Selenium has atomic number 34. Which is its ground-state electron configuration?
The photoelectron spectrum of a neutral atom shows four peaks. Moving from the highest binding energy to the lowest, their relative heights are 2 : 2 : 6 : 2. Which element is this?
Na+ and Mg2+ both have the electron configuration 1s2 2s2 2p6. Which statement correctly compares their radii and gives the reason?

choices.text: Mg2+ is larger, because magnesium has more protons and neutrons, so its nucleus takes up more space.
Na+ is larger, because it has an extra electron shell compared with Mg2+.
The ions are the same size, because identical electron configurations mean identical shielding and therefore identical radii.
Na+ is larger, because its 11 protons attract the same 10 electrons less strongly than the 12 protons of Mg2+ do.

rows.stem: Strontium is in Group 2 and nitrogen is in Group 15. Based on their valence electrons, what is the formula of the ionic compound they form?
Pauling electronegativities: H 2.20, C 2.55, Cl 3.16, Br 2.96, O 3.44. Which bond is polar covalent with the partial negative charge on the atom written second?

For a diatomic molecule AB, the potential energy is lowest at an internuclear distance of 140 pm, where it equals -390 kJ/mol. At 300 pm the potential energy is -25 kJ/mol, and it approaches 0 as the atoms move infinitely far apart. How much energy is needed to separate one mole of AB molecules into widely separated atoms, starting at equilibrium?
A crystal of sodium chloride shatters when struck sharply with a hammer, whereas a piece of copper just bends. Which explanation for the sodium chloride behavior is best?

choices.text: The ionic bonds are weak, so a small force separates the ions.
Sodium chloride is made of separate NaCl molecules that are held together only by weak forces and slip apart.
The delocalized electrons cannot flow when struck, so the lattice cracks.
The blow shifts one layer of ions so that like charges end up next to each other, and the resulting repulsion splits the crystal.

rows.stem: Approximate atomic radii (pm): Cu 128, Zn 134, Fe 126, Pd 137, W 139, C 77, H 53. Which pair of elements would most likely form a substitutional alloy?
How many valence electrons must appear in the Lewis diagram of the phosphate ion, PO4^3-?
Ozone, O3, has a bent structure with two equivalent resonance forms: O=O–O and O–O=O (lone pairs omitted). Which statement describes the two O–O bonds in a real ozone molecule?

choices.text: They are identical in length and strength, intermediate between a single bond and a double bond.
One bond is a double bond and the other a single bond, and the molecule rapidly switches between the two.
Both bonds are single bonds, because the double bond is only a drawing convention that is not used in real molecules.
Both bonds are full double bonds, because each oxygen needs to form two bonds to complete its octet.

rows.stem: A sample of HCl gas absorbs infrared radiation at a wavelength of 3.4 micrometers. This absorption is most directly evidence for which change in the molecules?

choices.text: An electron moving to a higher energy level
A change in the rotation of the molecule
A change in the vibration of the H–Cl bond
The removal of an electron from the molecule

rows.stem: A photon of light has a wavelength of 6.00 x 10^-7 m. Using h = 6.63 x 10^-34 J·s and c = 3.00 x 10^8 m/s, what is the energy of this photon?
Graphite and diamond are both network solids of pure carbon, yet graphite is soft and slippery while diamond is extremely hard. Which explanation is best?

choices.text: The covalent bonds between carbon atoms in graphite are much weaker than those in diamond.
In graphite, carbon atoms form strongly bonded layers, but the layers are held together only by weak forces and slide over one another; diamond is bonded covalently in all three dimensions.
Graphite is a metallic solid, so its atoms slide freely through a sea of electrons.
Graphite is a molecular solid made of separate C molecules held by weak intermolecular forces.

rows.stem: Window glass has particles arranged irregularly with no long-range repeating pattern, yet it holds a fixed shape. Which statement about glass is best supported at the particle level?

choices.text: It is a liquid, because its particles are arranged irregularly.
It is a solid, because its molar volume is much greater than that of a typical liquid.
It is a gas-like phase, because its particles are not locked in a regular crystal pattern.
It is a solid, because its particles are in close contact and only vibrate about fixed positions, even though they lack a repeating arrangement.

rows.stem: At 300 K and 500 atm, 1.00 mol of nitrogen gas occupies a larger volume than the ideal gas law predicts. Which explanation is best?

choices.text: Attractions between molecules grow stronger at high pressure and hold them together, which increases the volume.
At high pressure the molecules slow down, so they take up more room.
At this high pressure the molecules are packed so closely that their own volume is a significant part of the container, leaving less free space than the ideal gas law assumes.
The ideal gas law ignores molar mass, which becomes important only at high pressure.

Particulate diagram 1 shows 8 dissolved solute particles inside a box that represents 100 mL of solution. Diagram 2 shows 16 dissolved solute particles of the same solute inside a box that represents 200 mL of solution. How do the two solution concentrations compare?

choices.text: They are equal, because both have 0.08 solute particles per mL.
Solution 2 is more concentrated, because it has twice as many solute particles.
Solution 1 is more concentrated, because its box is smaller, so the particles look more crowded.
They cannot be compared, because the diagrams show different numbers of particles.

rows.stem: In paper chromatography, a mixture of two dyes is spotted on polar paper (the stationary phase) and a solvent (the mobile phase) moves up the paper. After the run, dye X has traveled 6.0 cm and dye Y has traveled 2.0 cm. Which statement best explains the separation?

choices.text: Dye X is attracted to the paper more strongly than dye Y, so the paper pulls it farther along.
Dye Y consists of larger particles that were caught in the pores of the paper, as in filtration.
Dye Y has no attraction to the solvent and dye X has no attraction to the paper, so each stays in one phase.
Dye Y interacts more strongly with the paper than dye X does, so it is held back and moves less far with the solvent.
